mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2.5% (FEDFUNDS < 2.5) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing the discount rate for equity valuation and generating positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through lower cost of capital for corporate investment.
failure_condition: The 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 2.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points (UNRATE rise > 0.3pp) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative 5-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The 5-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp over 3 months (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in housing starts (HOUST > 0.5%) and real sales of automobiles/furniture (RSAFS > 0.5%) indicate robust consumer demand, generating positive 60-day S&P 500 returns through elevated corporate revenue expectations and profit margins.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: The 60-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS increase > 0.5% over 1 month (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, industrial production (INDPRO) below 115.0 signals weakening supply capacity, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns through reduced corporate output and profit margin compression.
failure_condition: The 20-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO < 115.0 during late-cycle expansions (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals accelerating inflation, prompting monetary tightening that generates negative 5-day S&P 500 returns through higher discount rates and reduced equity attractiveness.
failure_condition: The 5-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% over 1 month (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Payroll employment above 130,000 thousand (PAYEMS > 130,000) indicates a strong labor market, supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth to produce positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS > 130,000 thousand (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, CPIAUCSL above 190.0 indicates persistent inflation, causing sustained high interest rates that generate negative 20-day S&P 500 returns through reduced equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: The 20-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 190.0 during monetary tightening cycles (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent industrial production (INDPRO) increase > 0.5% and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2.5% indicate robust economic activity under accommodative policy, generating positive 5-day S&P 500 returns through elevated corporate earnings and low discount rates.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS < 2.5 in 1 month
failure_condition: The 5-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO rises > 0.5% and FEDFUNDS < 2.5 over 1 month (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).
